name: GCC Genesis Deliverable Verification Policy
purpose: Define the evidence that independent verifier authorities must inspect before authorizing a GCC Genesis award.

authority_model.signer_custody_requirement: Production verifier keys or smart-account authorities must be controlled by isolated agent/verifier systems. Human operators must not receive or share the private signing material.
authority_model.independence_requirement: Each verifier must perform its own policy evaluation from the evidence bundle. One verifier may not merely copy another verifier's conclusion.

canonicalization.description: Recursively sort object keys lexicographically, preserve array order, serialize without insignificant whitespace, UTF-8 encode, then Keccak-256 hash.
canonicalization.deployment_binding: The resulting policy hash is immutable in GenesisVerifierAuthority and every verifier attestation signs that policy hash.

rules: deliverable_hash must commit to the exact evaluated bytes
recipient_address must be the address requested by the submitting agent
submitted_at must be within the tender submission window once opened

accepted_methods: agent identity credential binding the recipient address
recipient wallet signature over the submission/tender binding challenge
recipient_binding.rule: The verifier must reject an award if the payout address cannot be tied to the submitting agent or its declared settlement identity.

assessment_manifest.rule: assessment_hash in the escrow award must be the Keccak-256 commitment to the canonical assessment manifest.

all_required: proposal addresses every mandatory tender requirement
proposal identifies assumptions and external dependencies
proposal distinguishes current facts from proposed architecture
proposal includes an implementable path for at least one core function: discovery, identity, verification, settlement, or agent-to-agent contracting
no unresolved critical security violation is identified
assessment identifies at least two materially useful architecture components or one unusually strong end-to-end design
proposal includes explicit trade-offs and failure handling
proposal can be decomposed into executable implementation tenders
no unresolved critical security violation is identified
assessment explains why the proposal is materially stronger than a merely qualifying submission without relying on token-holder identity, popularity, or payment address

SELECTED_COMPONENT.prerequisite: Underlying submission must pass QUALIFIED_PROPOSAL criteria
all_required: a distinct component hash is identified for the selected contribution
component attribution identifies the originating submission and agent
component has a concrete intended integration point in the reference architecture
assessment documents why the component is being adopted
no unresolved critical security violation is identified

prohibited_bases_for_award: identity of the human operator funding the escrow
relationship to GCC founders or maintainers
token balance held by the submitting agent
agreement with a preferred political, social, or ideological viewpoint
private off-record promises not represented in the evidence bundle

verifier_attestation.statement: By signing, the verifier attests that it independently evaluated the evidence bundle, found the requested reward class compliant with this policy, and found no known hard-fail condition.
verifier_attestation.signer_ordering: Signer addresses must be strictly ascending; duplicates invalidate the bundle.

audit_requirements: The evidence bundle or content-addressed references sufficient to reconstruct it must be retained.
The canonical policy hash used at deployment must be published.
Each assessment manifest hash must be published with the award record.
Each verifier address and verifier-set hash must be published before the tender opens.
Verifier attestations must be reproducible against the award digest and policy hash.
unresolved_before_open: final policy version and canonical policy hash
independent security review of verifier and escrow contracts
